newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 18.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- American Home said it will pay $1.25 billion to acquire the 40 percent stake it doesn't already own in Genetics Institute.
- An Avondale team won a pact to build Navy amphibious-assault ships with an initial value of $641 million but a potential for billions more.
- Federal regulators are expected to adopt updated merger rules for electric utilities.
- The Fed left short-term interest rates unchanged.
- Texaco is expected to release a diversity program aiming to expand its minority work force.

- The Baby Bells and other local phone firms are heading into a lobbying fight in which they are almost certain to lose a chunk of the $23 billion they collect yearly for handling long-distance calls on their networks.
- Housing starts rose 9.2 percent in November.
- Dow Corning's creditors have nearly completed a rival bankruptcy reorganization proposal that could leave them with control of up to 95 percent of the company's common stock.
- Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz won U.S. approval for their $27 billion merger.
- LVMH said it completed most of its purchase of a controlling stake in DFS after an arbitrator brokered a truce among DFS's feuding shareholders.
- Home PC sales received a boost from price-cutting in the first two weeks of December.
- GTE has signed up over 750,000 customers for its long distance business.
- Four McDonnell Douglas officials and a former official sold $1.48 million of stock in October, missing out on the stock's almost 20 percent jump since Boeing announced plans to acquire the firm.
- Inflation indexed bonds may be a better deal than investors thought now that there's lots of talk in Washington about changing the way inflation is measured.
